mainTopic: The dispute between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל about canceling a גט's agents: the reasons for it, the "כּוּלְּכֶם" question, and how the הלכה is decided.
overview: This amud continues a ברייתא about a husband who told ten people to write a גט and then canceled in front of only some of them. רבי says the cancellation works, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says he must cancel in front of all ten. The first explanation is about testimony: if part of a group is cancelled, is the whole group cancelled? The second explanation is that something done in front of ten needs ten to undo it. The גמרא then asks what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל would say if the husband told them "all of you" must write it. It tries to answer from a ברייתא about two agents, but רב אשי pushes the proof off by saying that ברייתא is about delivery agents. The גמרא then turns to the practical הלכה. Through רבי אבא's two rulings, a story about רבי, and a story about רבי יאשיה of אושא, it concludes that canceling before a בית דין follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and the ten-agents case follows רבי. Finally, רב נחמן rules like רבי in both disputes, and the גמרא begins to challenge him from a statement of שמואל, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי's reasoning: the other agents are still valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining רבי's view. Partially cancelled testimony is not fully cancelled, so the agents who were not cancelled may still write and give the גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: [רבי holds that testimony that was partly cancelled] is not entirely cancelled. So if these other agents go and write the גט and give it, let them write and give it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its explanation of רבי's opinion in the ברייתא about a husband who told ten people to write a גט. It shows why he has no problem with a husband canceling in front of only some of the agents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי compares the ten agents to a group of witnesses. When part of a group is cancelled, the rest stay valid, so the agents who were not cancelled still have real שליחות. If they write and give the גט, it is a good גט, so nothing can go wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Testimony that was partly cancelled, for example because some of the witnesses were disqualified
Is completely cancelled
They write and give (the גט)
Let them write and let them give

steps.confusionAlert: "Testimony" here is a comparison. The ten people are agents to write a גט, but the גמרא treats them like a group of witnesses to work out what happens when only part of the group is cancelled.

phrases.english: is not entirely cancelled;
and if these others go
phrases.notes: "These" means the agents the husband did not cancel.

phrases.english: and write and give it,
let them write and give it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא בָּטְלָה כּוּלָּהּ; וְאִי אָזְלִי הָנָךְ כָּתְבִי וְיָהֲבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the גמרא's explanation of the dispute in the ברייתא about ten agents, which began on the previous amud.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי holds that partly cancelled testimony is not fully cancelled, so the remaining agents may validly write and give the גט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי, the agents who were not cancelled keep their שליחות.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reasoning: everyone is cancelled, but the rest don't know
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that partly cancelled testimony is fully cancelled. So canceling some agents cancels all of them. The others won't know this, and they may write a גט anyway, which would wrongly permit a married woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that testimony which was partly cancelled is entirely cancelled. These other agents do not know it, and they will go and write the גט and give it. Then people will permit a married woman to marry anyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the other side of the dispute. It shows why רבן שמעון בן גמליאל requires the husband to cancel in front of all ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, canceling part of the group cancels all of it, so every agent has lost his שליחות. But the agents who weren't there don't know that. They might write and deliver an invalid גט, and the woman would wrongly be treated as divorced while she is still an אשת איש. Canceling in front of everyone prevents that mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not know
And they permit
A married woman
To the world, meaning to marry anyone

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the two opinions are not only arguing about technical validity. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's rule is a safeguard against a serious mistake involving a married woman.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds:
testimony that was partly cancelled
is entirely cancelled;
and these others do not know,
phrases.notes: They don't know that their own agency was cancelled along with the others'.

phrases.english: and they go and write and give it;
and they permit a married woman to anyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל סָבַר: עֵדוּת שֶׁבָּטְלָה מִקְצָתָהּ בָּטְלָה כּוּלָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing side of the same explanation started in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that partly cancelled testimony is fully cancelled. Canceling some agents cancels all of them, and the ones who don't know might give an invalid גט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the husband must cancel in front of all the agents so they all know their שליחות has ended.

steps.title: Second explanation: what is done before ten needs ten to undo
steps.stepSummary: Another explanation: everyone agrees that partly cancelled testimony is not fully cancelled. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's real reason is that something done in front of ten people needs ten people to undo it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say this instead: everyone agrees that testimony which was partly cancelled is not entirely cancelled. Here, the reason of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is that he holds something done in front of ten people needs ten people to undo it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different way to explain the dispute. It removes the testimony argument completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first explanation, the two sides argued about testimony. Now both sides agree that the rest of the group stays valid. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's requirement comes from a separate idea: the husband appointed them in front of ten, so he can only undo it in front of ten.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say: introduces another explanation
Everyone agrees
A matter done in the presence of ten
To undo it, literally to pull it out

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to explain רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. (1) Partly cancelled testimony is fully cancelled, so the other agents might mistakenly give a גט. (2) Something done before ten needs ten to undo it.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
that everyone agrees that testimony that was partly cancelled
is not entirely cancelled;
and here, this is the reason
of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel:
he holds: a matter that is done in the presence of ten
needs ten to undo it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא עֵדוּת שֶׁבָּטְלָה מִקְצָתָהּ לֹא בָּטְלָה כּוּלָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the testimony-based explanation of steps 1–2 with a different reason for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both sides agree about testimony. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל requires ten because what was done before ten must be undone before ten.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A matter set up in the presence of ten needs ten to undo it, according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in this explanation.

steps.title: A new question: what if the husband said "all of you"?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל would hold if the husband told the ten that all of them must write the גט. It begins with one side: if his reason is about testimony, there is no risk here, since the others could never write it alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: if he said "all of you," what is the law? Maybe רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reason is that he holds partly cancelled testimony is entirely cancelled. These agents, since he told them "all of you," cannot write and give the גט on their own anyway.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about a case where the husband said "all of you." It begins laying out the first side, and the second side will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's worry is that the remaining agents might give a גט without knowing they were cancelled, that worry disappears when the husband said "all of you." Some of the group was cancelled, so the rest can't write it alone anyway. So according to this side, he could cancel in front of only some of them.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked: introduces an open question
All of you, meaning every one of the agents must take part
What is the law?
They are not able

steps.confusionAlert: This step gives only the first side of the question (the testimony reason). Step 5 gives the second side.

phrases.english: They asked:
If he said "all of you," what is the law?
phrases.notes: The husband told all ten that they must write the גט together.

phrases.english: Is the reason of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
because he holds:
testimony that was partly cancelled is entirely cancelled?
And these, since he told them "all of you,"
are not able to write and give it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the two explanations of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל from steps 2–3 to raise a case where they would lead to different results.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבן שמעון בן גמליאל still require canceling before all ten when the husband said "all of you"?

steps.title: The second side: what is done before ten needs ten to undo
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its question with the other possibility. Maybe רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reason is that anything done before ten needs ten to undo it, so even with 'all of you' he would require canceling in front of all ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reason is that he holds anything done in front of ten people needs ten people to undo it. If so, even when the husband said 'all of you,' the same rule applies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the question it opened in Step 4 by giving the second side. Now both possibilities are on the table, and the גמרא will look for proof next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 4, if the reason is testimony, saying 'all of you' removes the danger, so canceling in front of some would be enough. But if the reason is 'ten to do, ten to undo,' the danger does not matter at all. The husband appointed them as a group of ten, so he must cancel in front of all ten even when he said 'all of you.'

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps. This introduces the other side of a question.
In front of a group of ten
To pull it out, meaning to undo or cancel it
All of you. The case where the husband says all ten must write the גט together.

phrases.english: Or perhaps,
the reason of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
is because he holds:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל מִלְּתָא דְּמִתְעַבְדָא בְּאַפֵּי בֵּי עַשְׂרָה,
phrases.english: any matter that is done in front of ten people
needs ten people to undo it,
and therefore, even with "all of you" the same applies?
phrases.notes: Meaning: even when he said 'all of you,' he would still have to cancel in front of all ten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided question begun in Step 4 by giving the second side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבן שמעון בן גמליאל require canceling in front of all ten even when the husband said 'all of you'? The answer depends on whether his reason is testimony or 'ten to do, ten to undo.'

steps.title: Proof attempt from a ברייתא about two agents
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that when a husband tells two agents to give a גט, רבי lets him cancel one without the other present, while רבן שמעון בן גמליאל requires both to be together. Two agents are like 'all of you,' and yet they still argue. That suggests רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reason is 'ten to do, ten to undo.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If he said to two people, 'Give a גט to my wife,' he can cancel one without the other there. These are the words of רבי. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says he can cancel only when they are together. But two are just like 'all of you,' and still they argue!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to try to answer the question. It argues that two agents are the same as 'all of you,' and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל still requires canceling in front of both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two agents, neither one can act alone, so there is no risk that the one who did not hear the cancellation will act by himself. If רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reason were only that risk, he should agree with רבי here. Since he still argues, his reason seems to be that the cancellation must be done the same way the appointment was made.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. This introduces a source brought as proof.
One without the other being present
They are similar or equal to
And they argue

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If he said to two people: "Give a bill of divorce to my wife,"

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל לְבַטֵּל זֶה שֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי זֶה,
phrases.english: he can cancel it before this one, not in front of that one;
these are the words of Rabbi.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְבַטֵּל אֶלָּא זֶה בִּפְנֵי זֶה.
phrases.english: He can cancel only when this one is in front of that one.
But two are just like "all of you,"
phrases.notes: A גט needs two witnesses, so one agent could never do it alone. That makes it just like saying 'all of you.'

phrases.english: and yet they argue!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question from Steps 4-5 using a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reason is 'what is done before ten needs ten to undo,' so he requires full cancellation even with 'all of you.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about two agents, which are like 'all of you,' where רבן שמעון בן גמליאל still requires canceling in front of both.

steps.title: רב אשי: the ברייתא is about delivery witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the proof would work if the two were witnesses who write the גט. But the ברייתא may be talking about witnesses who deliver it, and either one of them could deliver alone, so the risk is still there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: If they were witnesses for writing, you would be right. But here we are dealing with witnesses for delivery.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי rejects the proof from Step 6 by saying the ברייתא is about a different kind of agent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing witnesses must both sign, so two of them really are like 'all of you.' Delivery agents are different, because one person can carry and hand over a גט alone. So the agent who did not hear the cancellation might still deliver it. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling in the ברייתא can therefore be explained by the testimony risk, and it proves nothing about 'all of you.'

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses of writing, who must sign the גט
Witnesses or agents of delivery, who bring the גט to the wife
Here, what are we dealing with? This introduces a narrower reading of a source.
So too, meaning 'yes, that would be right'

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
If it were about witnesses of writing, indeed so;
phrases.notes: He means: if so, your proof would work.

phrases.english: but here, what are we dealing with? Witnesses of delivery.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אִי בְּעֵדֵי כְתִיבָה – הָכִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from Step 6 by reading the ברייתא as a different case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the use of the ברייתא as proof. It does not decide the original question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the two agents could not act alone. Delivery agents can act alone, so they are not like 'all of you.'

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא supports רב אשי
steps.stepSummary: The end of the ברייתא says that if the husband appointed each agent separately, he may cancel each one alone. That fits delivery agents. Writing witnesses appointed separately should not count together at all, since witnesses must see the event together.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense, because the end of the ברייתא teaches: If he spoke to this one alone and to that one alone, he can cancel one without the other there. If you say it is about delivery witnesses, that works well. But if you say it is about writing witnesses, can they combine? Didn't the Master say that witnesses' testimony does not combine unless both see the event together?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רב אשי's reading from the last part of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the ברייתא describes two agents appointed at different times. If they were writing witnesses, they could not join together as a pair, because witnesses must see the event at the same time. So the ברייתא only makes sense if it is about delivery agents, which backs up רב אשי.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it makes sense. This introduces support for the last statement.
The end part of a משנה or ברייתא
It is fine if... This sets up 'this works, but that doesn't.'
They join together, here meaning to count as a pair of witnesses
That both see it as one, meaning at the same time

phrases.english: So too it makes sense,
since the end part teaches:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָזֶה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ וְלָזֶה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ –
phrases.english: If he spoke to this one alone and to that one alone,

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל לְבַטֵּל זֶה שֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי זֶה.
phrases.english: he can cancel before this one, not in front of that one.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא בְּעֵדֵי הוֹלָכָה – שַׁפִּיר;
phrases.english: It is fine if you say it is about witnesses of delivery, that works well;
but if you say it is about witnesses of writing,
do they join together?!
But the Master said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין עֵדוּתָן מִצְטָרֶפֶת, עַד שֶׁיִּרְאוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם כְּאֶחָד!
phrases.english: Their testimony does not join together until both of them see it as one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up רב אשי's reading in Step 7 using the end of the same ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's claim that the ברייתא is about delivery witnesses.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the ברייתא, read together with the rule that witnesses must see the event at the same time.

steps.title: Maybe the ברייתא follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה
steps.stepSummary: The support for רב אשי is pushed away. The ברייתא might follow רבי יהושע בן קרחה, who holds that witnesses can join even if they did not see the event together. If so, the סיפא could still be about writing witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps he holds like רבי יהושע בן קרחה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the support from Step 8. The ברייתא might follow a תנא who lets witnesses join even when they saw things separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 depended on the rule that witnesses must see the event at the same time. רבי יהושע בן קרחה disagrees with that rule. If the ברייתא follows him, writing witnesses appointed separately could still join, so the סיפא does not prove that the ברייתא is about delivery witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who holds that witnesses can join even if they did not see the event together
He holds, meaning this is his opinion

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about two agents could not settle the question. רב אשי reads it as delivery agents, and the support for his reading from the סיפא is pushed off by pointing to רבי יהושע בן קרחה. So the support fails, but רב אשי's answer still stands.
steps.confusionAlert: This last line does not reject רב אשי. It only rejects the extra support for him from the סיפא. His reading still stands as a possible answer.

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קָרְחָה סְבִירָא לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: Perhaps he holds like Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha.
phrases.notes: רבי יהושע בן קרחה holds that witnesses don't have to see the event together to count as a pair.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קָרְחָה סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the support brought in Step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the support from the סיפא. רב אשי's answer itself still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The support assumed that witnesses must see the event together, but רבי יהושע בן קרחה does not require this.

steps.title: Two rulings heard, but which is which was forgotten
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר יהודה reports that רבי אבא ruled once like רבי and once like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, but he does not remember which ruling went with which dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר יהודה said: I heard two rulings from רבי אבא. One followed רבי, and one followed רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. But I don't know which one followed רבי and which followed רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from 'what is the reasoning' to 'what is the practical הלכה.' This step sets up a puzzle that the next step will solve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate disputes between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל on our daf. רבי אבא split them: one goes like רבי, the other like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. The report is incomplete because we don't know which dispute goes with which ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: I heard from him (a reported teaching)
two (rulings)
one
I do not know
which one

phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda said:
I heard two rulings from Rabbi Abba:
one in accordance with Rabbi,
and one in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel;
and I do not know which is like Rabbi
and which is like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא יָדַעְנָא הֵי כְּרַבִּי וְהֵי כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from analyzing רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reasoning to deciding the practical הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה is split: one dispute follows רבי and the other follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, though the report does not say which is which.

steps.title: A story shows רבי changed his ruling to follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף solves the puzzle from a story brought by רב דימי. רבי first ruled that canceling before a בית דין works. When רבי פרטא protested, רבי switched to the view of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Let's figure it out ourselves. When רב דימי came, he said: there was a real case, and רבי ruled like the חכמים. רבי פרטא spoke up before him. He was the son of רבי אלעזר בן פרטא and the grandson of רבי פרטא the Great. He said: 'If so, what power does the בית דין have?' Then רבי went back and ruled like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף uses a real-life ruling to show which way the הלכה goes in the dispute about canceling a גט before a בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The protest 'what power does the בית דין have' is exactly רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reasoning. If a husband could still cancel a גט before a בית דין, the court's rule against doing so would mean nothing. Since רבי himself switched to that view, the cancel-before-בית-דין dispute is settled like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: let us look into it ourselves
a real case that happened
what power does the court have?
and he went back (reversed himself)

steps.whyThisMatters: A ruling given in a real case, and then reversed, is strong evidence for the practical הלכה.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Let us see for ourselves:
for when Rav Dimi came, he said:
There was an incident, and Rabbi acted according to the words of the Sages.
phrases.notes: The 'Sages' here hold that canceling before a בית דין works. That was רבי's own view at first.

phrases.english: Rabbi Perata said before him,

phrases.aramaic: בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן פַּרְטָא
phrases.english: the son of Rabbi Elazar ben Perata,

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי פַּרְטָא הַגָּדוֹל:
phrases.english: the grandson of Rabbi Perata the Great:

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, מָה כֹּחַ בֵּית דִּין יָפֶה?
phrases.english: If so, what power does the court have?
And Rabbi went back and acted
in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the uncertainty raised in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: Which dispute follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב דימי's report of a case in which רבי reversed himself after רבי פרטא's protest.

steps.title: So the 'ten people' dispute follows רבי
steps.stepSummary: Since the cancel-before-בית-דין dispute follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the other dispute must be the one that follows רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since this one follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, that other one follows רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the puzzle by elimination. The remaining dispute, about telling ten people to write a גט, goes like רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא's two rulings were split, one each way. Step 11 placed the cancel-before-בית-דין dispute with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, so the 'ten people' dispute must follow רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: and since this one
that other one

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב יוסף's solution of רבי אבא's two rulings, canceling a גט before a בית דין follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, because the court's rule must have power. The 'ten people' case follows רבי. (Step 16 brings רב נחמן, who disagrees and rules like רבי in both.)

phrases.english: And since this one is in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the dispute about canceling a גט before a בית דין.

phrases.english: that one is in accordance with Rabbi.
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the case of the husband who tells ten people to write a גט.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִדְּהָא כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, הָךְ כְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the remaining conclusion from step 11 by elimination.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Cancel-before-בית-דין follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל; the 'ten people' case follows רבי.

steps.title: רבי יאשיה of אושא also split the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds that רבי יאשיה of אושא also held one way like רבי and one way like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. It shows this with a story told by רבה בר בר חנה: רבי יאשיה made a man give a גט against his will and told the scribes to hide while writing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יאשיה of אושא also held that one הלכה follows רבי and one follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. As רבה בר בר חנה said: we were five elders sitting before רבי יאשיה of אושא. A certain man came before him, and he made the man order a גט against his will. He said to us: 'Go hide, and write it for her.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings extra support for the split הלכה from another sage. It begins a story whose details the גמרא will connect to both rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man was forced to divorce, so he might try to cancel the גט. רבי יאשיה told the elders to hide so the husband could not find them and cancel it. Steps 14 and 15 explain how his instructions match both rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: elders
he got a גט out of him
against his will
go hide yourselves

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה דְּמִן אוּשָׁא סָבַר,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoshiya from Usha also holds

phrases.aramaic: חֲדָא כְּרַבִּי וַחֲדָא כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.
phrases.english: one like Rabbi and one like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.
As Rabba bar bar Ḥana said:
We were five elders
sitting before Rabbi Yoshiya from Usha,
a certain man came before him,
and he got a bill of divorce out of him against his will.
phrases.notes: He means רבי יאשיה made the man agree to have a גט written, even though the man did not want to.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לַן: זִילוּ אִטַּמּוּרוּ וּכְתֻבוּ לַהּ.
phrases.english: He said to us: Go hide and write it for her.
phrases.notes: Hide so the husband can't find you and cancel the גט.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה דְּמִן אוּשָׁא סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings additional support from another sage for the split ruling in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That the הלכה follows רבי in one dispute and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the other.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה בר בר חנה's story about רבי יאשיה of אושא.

steps.title: Hiding the scribes shows רבי יאשיה holds like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל on canceling
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יאשיה held like רבי, the husband could cancel the גט without the scribes present, so hiding them would be useless. So he must hold like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think he holds like רבי, what good does hiding do? So learn from this that he holds like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first half of the story about רבי יאשיה. It proves which view he held in the dispute about canceling a גט away from the agents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי, a husband can cancel a גט even when the agents or scribes are not there. If so, hiding the scribes would not stop him, because he could cancel in front of anyone. Hiding only helps if canceling must happen in front of the scribes, which is the view of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: If it enters your mind (introduces a possibility the גמרא will reject)
They hide
What of it? (What would it help?)
He holds (this opinion)

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind that he holds like רבי,
then when they hide, what of it?
phrases.notes: Under רבי's view the husband could just cancel in front of other people, so hiding the scribes wouldn't stop him.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from it

phrases.aramaic: כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל סְבִירָא לֵיהּ;
phrases.english: that he holds like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ כְּרַבִּי, כִּי מִיטַּמְּרִי מַאי הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the story of רבי יאשיה brought in step 13 to extract his first ruling.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יאשיה holds like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the dispute about canceling a גט away from the agents
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יאשיה's instruction that the scribes hide while writing the גט

steps.title: Hiding rather than scattering shows he holds like רבי on the ten scribes
steps.stepSummary: If he also held like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the ten-scribes case, scattering would be enough. Since he told them to hide, he must hold like רבי there. So he ruled once like each.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think he holds like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the other case too, why do they need to hide? Let them just scatter! So learn from this: one ruling like רבי and one ruling like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second half of the story and concludes that רבי יאשיה split his rulings between the two תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ten-scribes case, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds the husband can only cancel in front of all of them together. If so, scattering would be enough, since he could never gather them all at once. Needing to hide shows he holds like רבי, that the husband can cancel before each scribe separately, so every scribe must be out of reach.

keyTerms.meaning: The other one (here, the other dispute)
To hide
Let them scatter
One (one ruling)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יאשיה, like רבי אבא, ruled like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל on canceling before a בית דין and like רבי on the ten scribes.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind that in the other case
he also holds like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל,
phrases.notes: The other case is the man who told ten people to write a גט for his wife.

phrases.english: why do they need to hide?
Let them just scatter!
Rather, learn from it:
one ruling is like רבי,
and one ruling is like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אִידַּךְ נָמֵי כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reading of the story begun in step 14 and draws the final conclusion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יאשיה held one way like רבי (ten scribes) and one way like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל (canceling before a בית דין).

steps.title: רב נחמן rules like רבי in both disputes
steps.stepSummary: רבא reports that רב נחמן holds the הלכה follows רבי in both disputes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב נחמן: the הלכה is like רבי in both cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third opinion about the הלכה. רב נחמן does not split; he rules like רבי in both disputes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, both רבי אבא and רבי יאשיה split their rulings. רב נחמן says a husband can cancel a גט even before a בית דין away from the agent, and can cancel before each scribe separately.

keyTerms.meaning: The final practical ruling
In both of them

phrases.english: And רבא said that רב נחמן said:
The הלכה is like רבי in both of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי בִּשְׁתֵּיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different ruling from the split approach of רבי אבא and רבי יאשיה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי in both the canceling-before-בית-דין dispute and the ten-scribes dispute.

steps.title: Doesn't רב נחמן accept the reasoning of ״מה כח בית דין יפה״?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן: he seems to accept the reasoning of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, as shown by something he said in the name of שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But doesn't רב נחמן hold the idea of ״what is the power of the court?״ Didn't רב נחמן say in the name of שמואל:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב נחמן's ruling and starts to bring a source against it. This step sets up the proof, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reason is that if a husband's cancellation still worked even though he broke the court's enactment against canceling this way, the court's power would mean nothing. The גמרא says רב נחמן seems to use this same reasoning elsewhere. If so, how can he rule like רבי, who rejects it?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the power of the court? (the court's actions must have force)
Doesn't he hold?
But didn't he say? (introduces a contradicting source)

phrases.english: But doesn't רב נחמן hold
"What is the power of the court?"
But didn't רב נחמן say that שמואל said:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵית לֵיהּ לְרַב נַחְמָן מָה כֹּחַ בֵּית דִּין יָפֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of רב נחמן just stated in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי in both disputes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן elsewhere, in the name of שמואל, seems to accept ״מה כח בית דין יפה״, the very reasoning of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. So he should not rule like רבי on canceling before a בית דין.
